describes: Linseed oil paint, the rule until about 1960: it mattes, chalks and thins to the grain, then scales in small flakes.

notes.chalk: How far a decade at full weather draws the coat towards its chalk: a flat, paler or greyer coat whose value goes towards towardValue (linear) and which keeps keepChroma of its colour; light colours drift grey, dark ones fade (the research). Linseed chalks most of the three. Judged by look.
notes.gloss: Smoothness when new and when old, and the years it takes to lose half the difference: a fresh oil coat has a soft sheen that goes in a few seasons. Judged by look.
notes.peel: Its loss at full weather begins onsetYears after the coat and is whole spanYears later; it goes in flakes about flakeMm across, alongGrain times longer along the board. Linseed scales late and small, a coat lasting 8-15 years before a repaint (the research). Judged by look.
notes.water: Its water profile as the town's (Shaders/Water.hlsl, Overstory.World.WaterPack): how much it darkens wet, how glossy its wet film, how long it holds water, how readily run-off stains it. An oil film sheds water but a chalked one drinks a little. Judged by look.
